chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Ibn Miskān, from Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr, who said:

A woman prays in three garments: an izār, a dirʿ, and a khimār, and it does not harm her that she cover herself with the khimār. If she does not find that, then with two garments: she wraps herself with one of them and covers herself with the other.

I said: And if it is a dirʿ and a milḥafah, and she does not have a head-covering upon her? He said: There is no problem if she covers herself with the milḥafah; and if it does not suffice her, then let her wear it lengthwise.

key_terms.خِمَارٍ: a head-covering used to cover the head and upper body
key_terms.دِرْعٍ: a long shirt or shift-like garment
key_terms.مِلْحَفَةً: an outer wrapping cloth or sheet

ai.seo_question: What garments may a woman wear for salat (prayer) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about the garments in which a woman may perform salat (prayer). It explains the minimum acceptable forms of covering in prayer and permits alternative arrangements when the usual garments are unavailable.
